answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a scarce resource before it may trade. Like a beacon planted in the tundra, a staking contract publicly attests that one identity controls one deposit, so splitting into many fake identities multiplies the cost instead of multiplying influence. Reputation accrues only to staked identities, and a jade tier of high-stake agents audits suspicious newcomers. An attacker must lock capital per fake identity and forfeits the stake if caught, so spawning sock puppets costs far more than any reward they could extract.
